antarctic_sea_ice_low.summary: Provisional NSIDC data show Antarctic winter sea‑ice extent at 17.59 million km², the third smallest since records began, sparking worries about a possible shift.
highlights: Antarctic sea‑ice maximum recorded on 14 September at 17.59 million km²
All five lowest July extents occurred since 2022 and four lowest August extents since 2023
Arctic minimum reached 4.60 million km² on 12 September, tying the joint‑10th lowest on record

pheland_mcdermid_prevalence.headline: Phelan‑McDermid Syndrome May Affect 1 in 7,300 People, Study Finds
pheland_mcdermid_prevalence.summary: A multisource analysis of 180,000 autism cases estimates Phelan‑McDermid syndrome prevalence at about 1 in 7,300, suggesting over 45,000 Americans may be undiagnosed.
highlights: Prevalence estimated at 13.7 cases per 100,000 people (≈1 in 7,300).
Analysis combined data from ten sources, including GeneDx, Labcorp, Ambry Genetics, and the SPARK study.
Researchers urge universal genetic testing for autism to uncover hidden cases and enable targeted clinical trials.

dna_metal_ion_bridging.headline: Scientists Visualize DNA Pairing and Reveal Metal Ions Drive Helix Alignment
dna_metal_ion_bridging.summary: Using atomic force microscopy, researchers captured DNA double helices pairing and showed positively charged metal ions facilitate their alignment.
highlights: Atomic force microscopy images display two DNA double helices nesting together
Computer simulations indicate metal ions bridge DNA backbones in the grooves
The findings support the long‑proposed DNA zipper model

retrograde_sub_neptune_red_dwarf.headline: Retrograde Sub‑Neptune GJ 3090 b Discovered Orbiting a Red Dwarf
retrograde_sub_neptune_red_dwarf.summary: Astronomers using ESO’s 3.6 m telescope measured the Rossiter‑McLaughlin effect and found GJ 3090 b orbiting its red dwarf star in a 136° retrograde tilt.
highlights: GJ 3090 b is a sub‑Neptune about 2.2 × Earth’s radius and 4.5 × Earth’s mass.
It completes an orbit every 2.9 days at 73 light‑years distance in the Phoenix constellation.
The measured orbital obliquity of ~136° makes it the first retrograde planet around an M‑dwarf.
Observations were made with the NIRPS spectrograph on ESO’s 3.6 m telescope detecting the Rossiter‑McLaughlin effect.

crispr_gene_drive_anopheles_gambiae.headline: CRISPR Gene Drive Alters Mosquito Transcriptome, Revealing Unexpected Molecular Effects
crispr_gene_drive_anopheles_gambiae.summary: RNA‑seq of Anopheles gambiae gene‑drive mosquitoes shows sex and diet drive most expression changes, but specific genotype‑linked transcripts are uniquely reduced.
highlights: Principal component analysis identified sex and blood‑feeding as primary transcriptomic drivers.
Gene‑drive mosquitoes showed decreased mRNA for histone H1, ficolin‑1, and E3 ubiquitin‑protein ligase XIAP.
Unique genotype‑specific expression changes suggest off‑target effects beyond the intended target gene.
Study used RNA sequencing of males on sugar, females on sugar, and blood‑fed females.

quantum_computer_space.headline: Quantum Processor Operates in Space for First Time on Satellite
quantum_computer_space.summary: A photonic quantum computer launched aboard a Falcon 9 satellite demonstrated Hong‑Ou‑Mandel interference in low‑Earth orbit, despite harsh space conditions.
highlights: The photonic chip achieved a Hong‑Ou‑Mandel visibility of 0.908, surpassing the classical limit of 0.5
Only three of six silicon single‑photon avalanche diodes remained functional after launch, requiring voltage adjustments
Radiation increased detector dark counts after 52 days, but the team compensated to recover signal

black_hole_jets_cgm.headline: Black‑hole jets illuminate galaxy halos, shaping star‑forming gas far beyond visible edges
black_hole_jets_cgm.summary: A study using DESI optical data and LOFAR radio observations shows that narrow jets from supermassive black holes ionize hydrogen in the CGM, brightening along jet paths and potentially throttling future star formation.
highlights: Jets from active supermassive black holes produce a directional H‑alpha glow in the circumgalactic medium
Combined DESI and LoTSS data from hundreds of galaxies reveal the signal only along jet axes
Brightest ionization occurs near the galaxy core and at the CGM’s outer edge, indicating energy deposition far out

quantum_simulation_matter_creation.headline: Duke Team Uses 13‑Ion Quantum Simulator to Recreate String‑Breaking Particle Creation
quantum_simulation_matter_creation.summary: Researchers at Duke University demonstrated a trapped‑ion quantum computer mimicking early‑universe particle formation, marking a key step for quantum‑physics simulations.
highlights: 13 trapped ions were programmed to emulate string‑breaking dynamics
The experiment, published in Nature Physics, matches classical computer predictions
International collaborators included University of Maryland, Oxford, Caltech, Cornell and KU Leuven

evidence_of_an_acetone_carboxylation_pat.headline: Arctic Photoheterotroph Porticoccus arcticus Uses Acetone Carboxylation to Fix CO₂
evidence_of_an_acetone_carboxylation_pat.summary: Genomic and metatranscriptomic data reveal that the Gammaproteobacterium Porticoccus arcticus harbors a highly expressed acetone carboxylation pathway in Arctic surface waters.
highlights: Acetone carboxylase genes were among the most abundant transcripts in metatranscriptomes from oligotrophic Arctic surface water.
Porticoccus arcticus comprised up to 9% of the microbial community in a multiyear 16S rRNA time series.
The bacterium possesses multiple proteorhodopsin genes acquired by lateral gene transfer, linking light harvesting to acetone
Genome analysis shows a streamlined genome yet retains the complete acetone carboxylation module.

rem_sleep_energy_paradox.headline: REM Sleep Paradox: Brain Fuel Rises While Neuronal ATP Drops During Dreaming
rem_sleep_energy_paradox.summary: Researchers at Tohoku University found that blood flow increases before REM sleep, yet neuronal ATP sharply declines, revealing an unexpected energy drain during dreams.
highlights: Blood volume in the brain rises about 50 seconds before REM onset, starting in the posterior cortex
Neuronal ATP levels fall as astrocytic pyruvate rises once REM sleep begins
Wide‑field fluorescence imaging of transparent‑skull mice captured real‑time metabolic shifts

microblazar_discovery.headline: Astronomers Spot First Microblazar Inside Milky Way Pointing Toward Earth
microblazar_discovery.summary: A tiny blazar, IR 18293‑0941, has been identified in our galaxy, offering a fast‑forward view of jet physics and a possible source of ultrahigh‑energy particles.
highlights: IRAS 18293‑0941 exhibits a one‑sided bright radio jet, the hallmark of a blazar.
Multi‑wavelength data from three observatories confirmed the source lies within the Milky Way.
The jet’s opposite‑directed shock may power the nearby ultrahigh‑energy particle hotspot.
The findings are detailed in a forthcoming Astronomy & Astrophysics paper after two decades of searching.

reinterpreting_2ga_carbon_signature.headline: Local Magma and Microbes May Explain 2‑Billion‑Year‑Old Carbon Signal
reinterpreting_2ga_carbon_signature.summary: A new Caltech study shows the famed Shunga‑Francevillian carbon‑isotope anomaly likely resulted from regional magma heating, hydrocarbon generation, and methane‑eating microbes rather than a global event.
highlights: The carbon‑isotope signal in the Zaonega Formation matches signatures of modern oil‑gas basins.
Magma intrusion heated sediments to ~350 °C, producing methane that was consumed by microbes.
Temperatures dropped to ~72 °C at an ancient seafloor asphalt spill, preserving the light isotope record.

mars_carbonate_rocks_model.headline: Underground Carbonates May Reveal Mars' Hidden Watery History
mars_carbonate_rocks_model.summary: A JAXA-led study shows that groundwater could bury carbonates deep beneath Mars, explaining the scarcity of surface carbonate rocks despite evidence of ancient water.
highlights: Feldspar-rich rocks can generate calcium/iron-rich carbonates under early‑Mars conditions.
Groundwater percolation forms carbonates more efficiently than standing water and can redeposit them at depth.
Simulations suggest vast underground carbonate reservoirs may exist, guiding future drilling missions.

crispr_ldl_2026.headline: Single CRISPR Dose Halves Bad Cholesterol for a Year in Trial
crispr_ldl_2026.summary: A one‑time infusion of CTX310 cut LDL cholesterol by 52.5% and triglycerides by 47.8% in 15 patients, with effects persisting after twelve months.
highlights: Highest dose (0.8 mg/kg) reduced LDL by 52.5% and triglycerides by 47.8% after 12 months
No serious adverse events were reported during the one‑year follow‑up
The therapy edits the ANGPTL3 gene in the liver to lower circulating blood fats

osiris_rex_bennu_sample_analysis.headline: OSIRIS‑REx Samples Reveal Bennu Formed at Solar System’s Snow Line
osiris_rex_bennu_sample_analysis.summary: Isotopic analysis of 120 g of Bennu regolith shows the asteroid originated from fine dust at the boundary between fire and ice, reshaping theories of early planet formation.
highlights: Isotopes of iron, titanium and chromium are uniformly mixed, indicating formation from fine‑grained dust
Water‑bearing minerals point to formation just inside the solar system’s snow line near Jupiter’s orbit
Bennu’s composition matches that of Ryugu and CI chondrite meteorites, suggesting a common birthplace

leg_bone_brain_recovery.headline: Pressing the Shinbone Boosts Survival and Recovery After Brain Injury in Mice and Pigs
leg_bone_brain_recovery.summary: Controlled compression of the shinbone activates bone cells that release protective blood signals, improving survival, movement and memory after severe brain trauma.
highlights: Repeated 300‑compression cycles on the shinbone increased mouse survival and reduced brain lesion size
PIEZO1‑deficient mice lost the protective effect, confirming a bone‑cell pressure sensor role
Serum from compressed‑bone mice transferred neuroprotection to untreated brain‑injured mice
Miniature pigs receiving shinbone pressure showed better behavioral scores and less neuronal loss

timema_evolution_predictability.headline: Predictable Color Shifts in Timema Stick Insects Reveal Limits of Evolution Forecasts
timema_evolution_predictability.summary: A 25‑year study of Timema cristinae shows that color‑morph frequencies can be modestly forecasted, while pattern‑morph changes follow highly predictable negative frequency‑dependent selection.
highlights: Color‑morph frequency changes achieved an r² of 0.14, indicating modest predictability.
Pattern‑morph frequencies reached an r² of 0.86, driven by negative frequency‑dependent selection.
The study combined 25 years of field observations, experimental manipulations, and genomic analyses.
Multiple selective pressures and climate variability reduced predictability for some traits.

glucosamine_alzheimer_2026.headline: Glucosamine Use Tied to 25% Faster Alzheimer’s Progression in Patients
glucosamine_alzheimer_2026.summary: A large UF Health record analysis links glucosamine supplementation with a 25% higher chance of mild cognitive impairment advancing to dementia, supported by mouse and tissue studies.
highlights: Glucosamine users showed a 25% increased risk of MCI progressing to dementia
In mouse models, glucosamine amplified protein sugar‑tagging and worsened social memory
Human Alzheimer’s brain tissue exhibited elevated hyperglycosylation compared with controls

medieval_grave_dna.headline: DNA Reveals Medieval Swedish Graves Were Often Not Family Burials
medieval_grave_dna.summary: Ancient DNA from 142 individuals shows adults and children buried together in medieval Sweden were rarely close relatives, highlighting social rather than kinship motives.
highlights: Genetic analysis of 142 people across Sigtuna, Västerhus and Fjälkinge found few close biological relatives sharing a grave
Boys and girls followed the same gender‑based burial patterns as adult men and women
Lady 56 was linked to parents, brother and daughters and buried with a scallop shell indicating a pilgrimage to Santiago de

2609_31465v1.headline: Dynamic Neutron Economy Shapes Late‑Time Cold r‑Process Peaks in Neutron Star Merger Ejecta
2609_31465v1.summary: Cold r‑process simulations reveal that post‑freeze‑out neutron exchange between second‑ and third‑peak nuclei actively sculpts the final abundance pattern.
highlights: Second‑peak nuclei (~A 130) become net neutron exporters early, while third‑peak (~A 195) and Rare‑Earth (~A 164) act as neutron
A competition between global neutron‑capture ‘push’ and beta‑delayed neutron ‘pull’ determines peak structures
Models overproduce odd‑even staggering in the third peak, implying β‑delayed neutron emission probabilities (Pₙ) are overestimated

2609_31106v1.headline: Fast Radio Bursts Reveal Hidden Cold Cloudlets in Cosmic Web
2609_31106v1.summary: A new arXiv pre‑print shows that scintillation of FRBs can expose tiny, cool cloudlets in filaments and the circumgalactic medium, constraining their volume‑filling fractions.
highlights: Filament and sheet plasma screens can suppress Milky Way scintillation for FRBs beyond redshift z ≈ 2–3.
Cold cloudlets in the CGM produce detectable scintillation signatures even for sources at z ≈ 0.5.
Predicted FRB sightline fractions depend on extragalactic dispersion measure, allowing constraints on cloudlet density, size
Volume‑filling fractions as low as f_v ≈ 10⁻⁵ could be probed for high‑redshift FRBs.

2609_31340v1.headline: High Lepton Asymmetry Limits Sterile Neutrino Dark‑Matter Production
2609_31340v1.summary: A large primordial lepton flavor asymmetry can saturate resonant sterile‑neutrino creation, capping dark‑matter abundance despite stronger matter potentials.
highlights: Resonant active‑sterile conversion is curtailed when delayed production overlaps active‑neutrino oscillations
Flavor‑asymmetry redistribution can nearly erase the lepton excess needed for sterile‑neutrino generation
Resulting saturation confines viable mixing angles to a two‑order‑of‑magnitude window in \(\sin^2(2\theta)\)
Pion condensation at extreme asymmetries may trigger a first‑order QCD transition and early‑Universe gravitational‑wave bursts

2609_30376v1.headline: New Simulations Reveal Unexpected Saturation Mechanism for Cosmic Ray Streaming Instabilities
2609_30376v1.summary: Fully kinetic PIC simulations show that gyro‑phase bunching, not nonlinear Landau damping, limits the growth of streaming instabilities driven by a shell‑distribution of cosmic rays.
highlights: Gyro‑phase bunching around driven Alfvén waves sets the saturation amplitude
Fluid‑PIC runs with ideal and Landau closures reproduce the same saturation level
Cosmic‑ray ions fully isotropize in the Alfvén‑wave frame regardless of damping model
Saturation amplitude remains unchanged when domain size is increased tenfold

2609_31178v1.headline: JWST Detects Methane Emission from Young Brown Dwarf LRL 11001 in IC 348
2609_31178v1.summary: Using high‑resolution JWST spectroscopy, astronomers identified 3.33 µm CH₄ emission from the ~6 MJup brown dwarf LRL 11001, revealing unexpected atmospheric chemistry.
highlights: Methane emission at 3.324 µm and 3.333 µm was observed for the first time in a young brown dwarf
The 3.4 µm absorption band matches large alkane (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂) signatures
Spectra were obtained at R ≈ 1000, improving on earlier R ≈ 100 observations
Emission likely originates in the photosphere rather than a circumstellar disk

2609_31081v1.headline: Set Transformer Unlocks Neutron Star Equation of State from Observations
2609_31081v1.summary: A permutation‑invariant Set Transformer model reconstructs the dense‑matter equation of state using variable‑size sets of neutron star masses, radii, and tidal deformabilities.
highlights: Model predicts pressure P(n) and sound‑speed c_s^2(n) on a fixed density grid with calibrated uncertainties
Self‑attention learns the star‑to‑density mapping directly from data
Accuracy improves with more observations and benefits especially from tidal‑deformability measurements

jwst_planet_formation.headline: JWST Shows Young Planetary Disks Lose Gas in Shifting Winds
jwst_planet_formation.summary: New JWST/MIRI observations of 72 Sun‑like stars reveal that magnetically driven jets give way to radiation‑driven winds as protoplanetary disks age, tightening the window for gas‑giant formation.
highlights: Molecular hydrogen winds dominate in the youngest disks, detected in 46 of 72 systems
Ionized neon jets appear as disks mature, found in 40 systems
Photoevaporation becomes the primary gas‑loss mechanism once magnetic jets fade

antimicrobial_peptides_160myr.headline: 160-Million-Year-Old Lactoferrin Peptides Outperform Modern Counterparts Against Superbugs
antimicrobial_peptides_160myr.summary: Scientists reconstructed ancient lactoferrin antimicrobial peptides dating back 160 million years and found several to be more potent against drug‑resistant bacteria than today’s human versions.
highlights: Reconstructed peptides span from Jurassic ancestors to recent mammals using ancestral sequence reconstruction
Some 160‑million‑year‑old peptides showed greater killing of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus than modern human
A single amino‑acid mutation accounted for the increased potency of newer ancestral peptides
Study published in PLOS Biology (Aug 2026) and funded by the National Institutes of Health

metal_free_mri_contrast.headline: Metal‑Free Molecules Emit Deep‑Red Light and Boost MRI Contrast
metal_free_mri_contrast.summary: Researchers at Kyushu University created water‑soluble, metal‑free radicals that fluoresce deep red and enhance MRI contrast up to 4.5‑fold in test phantoms.
highlights: TTM‑trisTP3B and TTM‑trisTP9B show deep‑red fluorescence lasting at least 24 hours in cells
MRI signal intensity increased 2.5–4.5 times compared with earlier water‑soluble TTM radicals
Both molecules combine fluorescence imaging and MRI contrast without any paramagnetic metal

atom_light_graph_framework_2026.headline: Graph Theory Maps Atom‑Light Interaction, Revealing Unlimited Quantum State Network
atom_light_graph_framework_2026.summary: A new magnetic‑graph framework unifies weak to deep‑strong atom‑light coupling, showing a semi‑infinite network of quantum states and a single metric to classify regimes.
highlights: Researchers Sunkyu Yu, Namkyoo Park, and Xianji Piao introduced a “magnetic graph” theory for cavity QED.
The graph treats quantum states as nodes and transition amplitudes as weighted, colored links, exposing a semi‑infinite
A magnetic Laplacian metric compresses the entire coupling spectrum into one continuous number.
Phase frustration, not just connectivity, drives the restructuring of states in ultrastrong and deep‑strong regimes.

greenland_valleys_map.headline: New Ice Flow Analysis Reveals Hidden Valley Network Beneath Greenland Ice Sheet
greenland_valleys_map.summary: Scientists used Ice Flow Perturbation Analysis to map 1,943 subglacial valleys, uncovering a complex landscape that reshapes our understanding of Greenland’s geology.
highlights: Mapped 1,943 subglacial valleys, about one‑third newly identified
Valleys extend hundreds of kilometres inland, revising BedMachine Greenland data
Straight, southwest‑northeast‑aligned valleys suggest tectonic control
Wide branching angles imply ancient groundwater erosion before ice coverage

magnetic_order_gapless_magnets.headline: Magnetic Order Persists in Gapless 2D Random‑Bond Ising Magnets
magnetic_order_gapless_magnets.summary: A new proof shows that ferromagnetism survives weak quantum fluctuations in the gapless random‑bond quantum Ising model, confirming a long‑standing conjecture.
highlights: Researchers proved robust symmetry breaking in a 2D random‑bond Ising model without an energy gap
The quantum Peierls condition shows system‑spanning domain walls remain energetically costly
The work, published in Physical Review Letters, uses a novel adaptation of the classic Peierls argument

mars_warm_region.headline: Mars’ Southern Mantle Holds a 200‑400°C Warm Spot Revealed by Tidal Tomography
mars_warm_region.summary: Using 16 years of orbiter data, researchers identified a mantle region in Mars’ southern highlands that is 200‑400°C hotter than surrounding areas.
highlights: The warm anomaly was detected through tiny speed changes of the Mars Global Surveyor, Mars Odyssey, and Mars Reconnaissance
Tidal tomography shows the region may cause partial melting but is stalled by the thick southern crust
The discovery suggests a compositional component similar to Earth’s Large Low Shear Velocity Provinces

fossil_mammal_lineage_discovery.headline: Gobi Desert Fossil Overturns 40‑Year View of Cretaceous Mammal Lineage
fossil_mammal_lineage_discovery.summary: A near‑complete Cretaceous mammal fossil from Mongolia shows zhelestids belong to the zalambdalestoid group, not early placental relatives.
highlights: Tamirkhan balcarceli is the most complete zhelestid specimen yet discovered
Its long hind limbs and ankle structure match zalambdalestoid traits
Teeth alone misled researchers for decades about zhelestid relationships

ancient_human_face_morocco.headline: Digital Reconstruction Gives Face to 315,000-Year-Old Homo sapiens from Morocco
ancient_human_face_morocco.summary: Scientists used open‑source 3D techniques to assemble fossil fragments from Jebel Irhoud, creating grayscale and full‑color facial models of an ancient Homo sapiens.
highlights: Composite skull assembled from Irhoud 1 and additional jaw fragments dated ~315,000 years
Digital facial approximation produced both anatomy‑focused grayscale and lifelike full‑color versions
Estimated brain volume of 1,364 mL (1,230 cm³) falls within modern human male range
Reconstruction relied on African ancestry soft‑tissue datasets and open‑access Max Planck Institute imagery

darkside_ultraheavy_nuclear_dm_2026.headline: DarkSide-50 Rules Out Ultraheavy Nuclear Dark Matter in Seven‑Year Search
darkside_ultraheavy_nuclear_dm_2026.summary: The DarkSide collaboration’s seven‑year DarkSide-50 run found no signals of composite ultraheavy dark matter, tightening constraints on its possible internal structure.
highlights: No evidence of composite dark matter interacting with liquid argon.
The analysis incorporated dark‑matter form factors, allowing a single particle to scatter multiple times.
Results exclude a broad range of ultraheavy dark‑nucleon masses, sharpening future search targets.
DarkSide-20k, planned for 2027 with roughly 1,000 × more liquid argon, will probe potential “dark chemistry” signatures.

shared_dna_switch.headline: Hybrid DNA promoter works in both E. coli and yeast
shared_dna_switch.summary: KAIST scientists created a hybrid promoter that activates genes in both Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae, enabling comparable control of compound production.
highlights: The hybrid promoter combines DNA elements recognized by both bacteria and yeast
Promoter strength rankings were preserved across the two hosts
Using a three‑gene green pigment pathway, output increased 3.1‑fold in E. coli and 2.6‑fold in yeast

zebrafish_albinism_gene_role.headline: Zebrafish Study Shows OCA2 Gene Impacts Eye Development Beyond Pigment Production
zebrafish_albinism_gene_role.summary: Mutations in the OCA2 gene alter pigment cell patterns, eye formation, and gene activity in zebrafish embryos, hinting at broader developmental roles.
highlights: OCA2 mutations changed iridophore numbers and locations in zebrafish embryos
Eye closure was delayed and retinal cell organization was altered in mutants
Transcriptomic analysis revealed dozens of downstream genes affected

hydrogen_glow_dark_energy.headline: CHIME Detects Distant Hydrogen Glow, Opening New Path to Probe Dark Energy
hydrogen_glow_dark_energy.summary: For the first time, the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment captured the faint 21 cm signal from 5 billion‑year‑old hydrogen, offering a cheaper, large‑scale method to study dark energy.
highlights: CHIME mapped the 21 cm autocorrelation at redshift z ≈ 1 using 94 nights of 2019 data
The signal shows roughly 2 % of cosmic hydrogen was neutral, matching prior measurements
This technique bypasses costly galaxy surveys, enabling cheaper, broader cosmological studies

lunar_magnetic_fossil_change_6.headline: Lunar γ‑Fe Nanoparticles Reveal Ancient Magnetic Fossil in Chang’e‑6 Samples
lunar_magnetic_fossil_change_6.summary: Researchers identified face‑centered cubic γ‑Fe in Chang’e‑6 impact‑glass, showing it can retain a stable magnetic vortex that records the Moon’s early field.
highlights: First natural lunar samples found to contain face‑centered cubic γ‑Fe
γ‑Fe nanoparticles exhibit a single‑vortex magnetic state stable under external fields
Impact‑glass cooling and trace carbon may preserve the high‑temperature γ‑Fe phase
Discovery expands known magnetic minerals that can archive lunar impact history

automated_lnp_production.headline: MIT Automates Lipid Nanoparticle Production to Speed RNA Therapy Development
automated_lnp_production.summary: MIT researchers have created an automated two‑step mixing platform that precisely controls lipid nanoparticle size and shape, accelerating RNA therapeutic design.
highlights: Automated system uses dynamic light scattering to verify particle size in real time
Residence‑time adjustments enable production of 70 nm to 150 nm particles and avocado‑shaped LNPs
Machine‑learning model predicts optimal mixing parameters for desired size or shape

altermagnetism_layered_material.headline: Layered Co₁/₄TaSe₂ Shows First Experimental Altermagnetism, Boosting Spintronics
altermagnetism_layered_material.summary: Researchers at University of Central Florida have experimentally confirmed altermagnetic spin‑splitting in the layered material Co₁/₄TaSe₂, offering a new platform for spintronic devices.
highlights: ARPESand spin‑resolved ARPES revealed opposite spin polarizations in split electronic bands of Co₁/₄TaSe₂.
The material avoids stray magnetic fields while generating spin currents, combining ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic
Experiments were performed at the Advanced Light Source and Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource, confirming theoretical

water_stable_catalyst.headline: Water‑Stable Ruthenium Catalyst Extends Olefin Metathesis to Living Cells
water_stable_catalyst.summary: A newly designed ruthenium catalyst with a cyclic (alkyl)(amino) carbene ligand remains active for up to 600 cycles in aqueous environments, enabling bioconjugation.
highlights: Ruthenium catalyst featuring a CAAC ligand shows unprecedented water stability
Integrated aniline group allows selective attachment to proteins and peptides
Catalyst retains activity for up to 600 reaction cycles in biological media

forests_drought_co2_absorption.headline: Drought Forces Forests to Lose Their Carbon‑Absorbing Power
forests_drought_co2_absorption.summary: When water scarcity forces trees to close stomata, photosynthesis halts and forests can switch from carbon sinks to net CO₂ emitters.
highlights: Forests normally capture about a quarter of anthropogenic CO₂ emissions
Each CO₂ molecule absorbed requires roughly 400 water molecules to be released
Severe drought triggers stomatal closure, halting photosynthesis and causing forests to emit CO₂
Species‑specific hydraulic vulnerability determines how quickly trees shut down water transport
Reduced transpiration can diminish regional rainfall, as seen in the Amazon basin

neurodegeneration_tcells.headline: Blocking CXCR3 Keeps T Cells Out, Slowing Mouse Neurodegeneration
neurodegeneration_tcells.summary: A Washington University study shows that an antibody blocking CXCR3 prevents T‑cell entry into mouse brains, reducing tissue loss by 40% and improving memory.
highlights: Antibody targeting CXCR3 stopped T‑cell accumulation in hippocampal regions.
Treated mice exhibited 40% less brain tissue loss in memory‑related areas.
Cognitive performance improved on standard memory tests despite unchanged tau levels.
Findings published in Neuron using preclinical mouse models of tauopathies.

polymer_tuned_perovskite_underwater_sola.headline: Polymer‑tuned perovskite solar cell achieves 34.71% efficiency at 10 m depth
polymer_tuned_perovskite_underwater_sola.summary: A Yunnan University team engineered a wide‑bandgap perovskite with polymer additive PHMG, delivering record 34.71% power conversion efficiency in simulated deep‑water light.
highlights: Wide‑bandgap perovskite tuned to 1.96 eV matches blue‑green underwater spectrum
Polyhexamethylene guanidine hydrochloride (PHMG) raises ion‑migration barrier from 0.07 eV to 0.21 eV
Underwater module generated 324 mWh at 10 m depth, powering LEDs in the South China Sea

iron_minerals_water_storage.headline: Iron Oxyhydroxide Minerals May Store Primordial Water Deep in Earth
iron_minerals_water_storage.summary: Newly identified iron oxyhydroxide minerals can hold up to 15% water by weight, offering a possible source for Earth's early oceans.
highlights: Minerals stable at core‑mantle boundary pressures exceeding one million atmospheres
Each mineral contains up to 15% water by weight, equivalent to a pint in a five‑pound piece
Dense enough to sink, they could transport water from the deep mantle to surface volcanic hotspots
Discovery published in Nature Geoscience provides the first concrete reservoir model for mantle water

microbial_profiling_method.headline: New Metax Profiler Cuts Through Contamination to Reveal True Microbial Signals in Low‑Biomass Samples
microbial_profiling_method.summary: A novel taxonomic profiler called Metax, developed by researchers at Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research, more reliably distinguishes genuine microbes from contamination in scarce‑DNA samples.
highlights: Metax uses genome‑wide read distribution to separate true signals from kitome artifacts
Improved identification and abundance estimates were shown across bacteria, archaea, fungi, viruses, and eukaryotes
Tests on human microbiome, wastewater and clinical samples demonstrated higher accuracy than existing profilers

salmon_genome_duplication.headline: Whole-Genome Duplication Drove Salmon Evolution Over 100 Million Years
salmon_genome_duplication.summary: A new EU‑funded study mapped gene activity in Atlantic salmon and rainbow trout, revealing how ancient genome duplication still shapes their development and traits.
highlights: The salmonid ancestor underwent whole‑genome duplication ~100 million years ago.
Researchers generated ~800 high‑quality sequencing datasets, totaling 80 billion DNA‑sequence pairs.
Gene expression is most constrained during late embryonic development, limiting evolutionary change.
The AQUA‑FAANG project, a €6 million EU collaboration, made the data freely available for future research.

pacific_water_paradox.headline: Pacific Thermocline Shows Paradox: Young Water Ages, Old Water Rejuvenates
pacific_water_paradox.summary: A simplified circulation model predicts that warming will slow vertical mixing, causing younger Pacific thermocline water to age while older deep water becomes younger.
highlights: Warming reduces density differences, weakening exchange between surface layer and thermocline at 200–1,000 m depth.
In the subtropical North Pacific, slower mixing makes the thermocline water older; in the tropical Pacific, it becomes younger.
The slowdown is linked to heat forcing from the Southern Ocean, affecting vertical velocities across the basin.

ocean_chemistry_life_breathing.headline: Ancient Ocean Chemistry Fueled Oxygen Rise After Great Oxidation Event
ocean_chemistry_life_breathing.summary: Researchers show that phosphorus recycling in early oceans created a feedback loop that kept atmospheric oxygen high for millions of years.
highlights: Phosphorus released from sulfate‑driven microbes boosted marine productivity
New mineral‑specific phosphorus analysis of South African rocks revealed bioavailable nutrient levels
The feedback loop sustained oxygen after the Great Oxidation Event ~2.3 billion years ago

room_temp_superconductor_scandium.headline: Scandium’s 3d Electrons Unlock Room‑Temperature Superconductivity in LaSc₂H₂₄
room_temp_superconductor_scandium.summary: Researchers at Jilin and Zhejiang Universities explain why LaSc₂H₂₄ superconducts at 43 °C under 167 GPa, pinpointing scandium’s 3d electrons as the key.
highlights: LaSc₂H₂₄ achieves a critical temperature of 43 °C at 167 GPa
Scandium’s 3d electrons reshape the Fermi surface, eliminating anisotropic superconductivity channels
Replacing Sc with Ca or Mg removes superconductivity, confirming the essential role of 3d orbitals

exoplanet_weather_simp0136.headline: Irish team uses JWST to decode weather on distant brown dwarf SIMP 0136
exoplanet_weather_simp0136.summary: Researchers at Trinity College Dublin applied a new Principal Component Analysis technique to JWST data, revealing temperature‑driven cloud structures shaping the atmosphere of the 20‑light‑year‑distant object.
highlights: SIMP 0136, a ~13 Jupiter‑mass rogue planet, shows three recurring weather states driven by temperature and cloud‑layer changes
Principal Component Analysis isolates dominant atmospheric patterns from minute brightness variations as the object rotates
The method, validated on high‑quality JWST observations from 2023, can be applied to other brown dwarfs and giant exoplanets

feathered_dinosaur_discovery.headline: Four‑winged dinosaur Norellraptor barsboldi sheds light on independent flight evolution
feathered_dinosaur_discovery.summary: A 57‑cm microraptor named Norellraptor barsboldi from the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation shows convergent flight traits, supporting multiple origins of avian‑like flight.
highlights: N. barsboldi measured 57 cm and died at three years old, preserving four wings and sharp predatory teeth.
About 30 % of 194 anatomical changes in microraptors parallel those in early birds, including a longer ulna than humerus.
The study, published in Nature Communications, shows the sequence of trait evolution differed between microraptors and Avialae.
Researchers Andrea Cau and team used comparative analysis to argue flapping flight arose independently in non‑avialan dinosaurs.

gene_therapy_huntington.headline: UniQure’s AMT-130 Gene Therapy Slows Huntington’s Progression Four Years Post‑Implant
gene_therapy_huntington.summary: Four years after brain implantation, UniQure’s one‑time gene therapy AMT‑130 reduced Huntington’s disease progression by 44% versus an external control cohort.
highlights: High‑dose AMT‑130 achieved a 44% slower decline in motor and cognitive scores
Benefit magnitude decreased compared with the one‑year follow‑up analysis
The difference did not reach statistical significance
Data derived from matched participants in a large natural‑history study

galaxies_cosmic_house_mirrors.headline: Webb Reveals Mirror‑Warped Galaxies in Distant Cluster MACS J0454.1‑0300
galaxies_cosmic_house_mirrors.summary: James Webb Space Telescope images show gravitationally lensed galaxies magnified over 300‑times, exposing structures from 800 million to 2 billion years after the Big Bang.
highlights: The cluster MACS J0454.1‑0300 lies at a redshift corresponding to when the Universe was ~8 billion years old.
Lensing by the cluster creates multiple arcs, revealing a galaxy group 2 billion years after the Big Bang and a single galaxy
Individual star‑forming knots as small as 5 light‑years are magnified by more than 300×.
Webb’s infrared sensitivity uncovers hundreds of galaxies missed by the 2014 Hubble image.
Data derive from JWST programmes #5058 (PI Furtak) and #6882 (PI Fujimoto).

haumea_core_2026.headline: Haumea’s Dense Rocky Core Unveiled by Satellite Dynamics
haumea_core_2026.summary: Analysis of two decades of Hubble Space Telescope astrometry shows the dwarf planet Haumea possesses a dense rocky core beneath an ice‑rich mantle.
highlights: Dynamical model fits Hubble astrometry to measure Haumea’s J₂ and satellite masses
Combined J₂ and occultation shape data confirm a rocky core overlain by ice mantle
Results suggest frozen‑in fossil figure but more data are needed

2609_35974v1.headline: JWST Survey of 29 Lensed Quasars Finds Hints of Self‑Interacting Dark Matter
2609_35974v1.summary: A study of 29 quadruply imaged quasars using JWST shows a strong preference for core‑collapsed halos, challenging the standard cold dark matter model.
highlights: Core‑collapsed halos favored with Bayes factors ranging from 6:1 to 24:1
Analysis spans halo masses from 10⁶ to 10¹⁰·⁷ M☉
Explaining the data without collapse would require unusually high globular‑cluster counts and excess subhalos

alpine_cristal_jwst_survey_high_z_resolv.headline: ALPINE‑CRISTAL‑JWST Survey Maps Dust, Gas and Stars in z~4‑5 Galaxies at Kiloparsec Scales
alpine_cristal_jwst_survey_high_z_resolv.summary: A new study combines ALMA and JWST/NIRSpec IFU data to resolve gas, dust and stellar distributions in high‑redshift galaxies, revealing varied metallicities and feedback effects.
highlights: Spatially resolved [CII] and dust continuum observations trace atomic and molecular gas across ~kpc scales
Oxygen abundance maps show 12+log(O/H) values of 8.1‑8.3 with up to 1 dex internal variation
Galaxies with strong outflows exhibit lower dust‑to‑stellar surface density ratios and reduced gas fractions
A revised [CII] conversion factor yields more accurate total gas mass estimates than previous calibrations
Some z~4‑5 galaxies possess dust‑to‑gas ratios an order of magnitude higher than local counterparts

2609_36632v1.headline: Unified Limits on Cosmic Neutrino Flux Across Ten Decades of Energy
2609_36632v1.summary: A new analysis combines data from Cherenkov telescopes, air‑shower arrays, and radio detectors to set 90% C.L.
highlights: Reconstructed energy‑dependent exposures from multiple experiments into a common all‑flavor ν+ν̄ framework
Applied a Poisson likelihood to merge event counts and backgrounds, yielding quasi‑differential limits
Used the combined exposure to constrain cosmogenic neutrino models and selected new‑physics scenarios

full_dataset_search_for_solar_wimp_annih.headline: ANTARES Sets Stronger Limits on Solar Dark Matter Annihilation
full_dataset_search_for_solar_wimp_annih.summary: Using data from 2007‑2022, ANTARES found no solar neutrino excess, tightening WIMP‑proton cross‑section limits for masses 35 GeV to 10 TeV.
highlights: Full ANTARES dataset (2007‑2022) analyzed for solar neutrinos
No significant excess observed over background
Upper limits placed on spin‑dependent and spin‑independent WIMP‑proton interactions
Limits improve previous ANTARES results by a factor of two‑three

crystal_spacing_magnetic_states.headline: Lattice Spacing Outperforms Electron Count in Predicting Magnetism of Complex Alloys
crystal_spacing_magnetic_states.summary: A study of Au‑based Tsai‑type approximants shows that the lattice parameter reliably predicts antiferromagnetic, ferromagnetic and spin‑glass states, surpassing the traditional e/a ratio.
highlights: Magnetic ground states align with lattice parameters: >14.72 Å (AFM), 14.62‑14.72 Å (FM), <14.62 Å (spin‑glass).
The inverse correlation between e/a ratio and lattice parameter was confirmed across Tb, Dy and Ho samples.
The unified magnetic phase diagram offers a practical roadmap for designing new quasicrystal‑based magnetic materials.

first_stars_simulations.headline: MEGATRON Simulations Show First Stars Light Up Universe and Seed Elements
first_stars_simulations.summary: Ultra‑detailed MEGATRON simulations reveal how the earliest stars illuminated the dark cosmos and forged carbon, oxygen and iron that later formed planets and life.
highlights: MEGATRON links JWST galaxy observations with chemical fingerprints in ancient Milky Way stars
Simulations track gas dynamics, starlight, and element enrichment from pristine gas to supernovae
High‑resolution models capture gas structures missed by simpler approaches

300tevphoton.headline: 300 TeV Photon from GRB 221009A Challenges Standard Physics
300tevphoton.summary: A photon‑like event of 300 TeV detected after GRB 221009A may require axion‑like particles or Lorentz‑invariance violation to explain its survival across the cosmos.
highlights: Carpet detector recorded a 300 TeV photon‑like event with only 3 × 10⁻⁴ chance of misidentifying a hadron
ALP conversion can aid photons up to ~20 TeV but falls short by two orders of magnitude at 300 TeV
Lorentz‑invariance violation could raise the photon‑photon absorption threshold, making the universe more transparent at

dinosaurseaweeddiet.headline: Dinosaur Teeth Reveal Seaweed Consumption Along Ancient North American Coastlines
dinosaurseaweeddiet.summary: Isotope analysis shows coastal dinosaurs and crocodiles incorporated marine macroalgae into their diets, confirming marine subsidization in Cretaceous ecosystems.
highlights: δ13C values in coastal fossil teeth are consistently higher than those from inland sites
Study examined fossils from early Albian (113–107 Ma) and early Cenomanian (100–96 Ma) deposits
Marine macroalgae identified as the most likely source of extra carbon across the food chain
Tenontosaurus tilletti showed no marine signature, indicating dietary variation

2609_35941v1.headline: JWST Finds Massive Pop III Galaxies Near GN‑z11 Analog, Shaped by Baryon‑Dark Matter Streaming
2609_35941v1.summary: A semi‑analytic model applied to a zoom‑in N‑body simulation shows that high streaming velocities allow late‑forming Population III galaxies to survive near the bright GN‑z11‑like galaxy.
highlights: Pop III and metal‑enriched star formation start earlier and at higher rates in the overdense region
Late‑forming Pop III galaxies appear near the central galaxy due to ionizing feedback and strong Lyman‑Werner radiation
Higher baryon‑dark matter streaming velocity (v_bc) preserves chemical pristine‑ness, enabling these galaxies, absent when v_bc=0

antarctica_ice_loss_locked.headline: Antarctica’s Ice Loss Locked In Even With 1.5°C Target
antarctica_ice_loss_locked.summary: A new Nature Geoscience study shows Antarctica will shed more ice than it gains this century, despite extra snowfall and a 1.5 °C warming limit.
highlights: Antarctica will lose more ice than it gains even if global warming stays below 1.5 °C
Machine‑learning analysis of ISMIP6 simulations identified three key physical assumptions driving sea‑level rise
Projected Antarctic contribution could add up to 10 inches (25 cm) of sea level by 2100, threatening over 10 million coastal

retrograde_exoplanet_discovery.headline: Retrograde Exoplanet GJ 3090 b Spins Backward Around M Dwarf
retrograde_exoplanet_discovery.summary: Astronomers using NIRPS at La Silla discovered GJ 3090 b orbiting its M dwarf star in a 136° retrograde path, challenging planet‑formation models.
highlights: GJ 3090 b completes an orbit every 2.9 days
The planet’s orbit is misaligned by 136 degrees with the star’s spin
23 hours of NIRPS observations captured ten transits
No massive companions were found to explain the retrograde motion

record_breaking_x_ray_flash_magnetar.headline: Record-Breaking Ten-Minute X‑Ray Flash Signals Birth of a Magnetar
record_breaking_x_ray_flash_magnetar.summary: Astronomers observed a ten‑minute X‑ray flash from a neutron‑star merger, providing strong evidence that the collision created a rapidly spinning magnetar.
highlights: The flash, designated EP250704a/GRB 250704B, lasted nearly ten minutes—longer than any previously recorded prompt X‑ray emission
VLT X‑Shooter spectra gave a redshift of z=0.6610, placing the event over six billion light‑years away
No accompanying supernova was detected, supporting a neutron‑star merger origin rather than a massive‑star collapse

homo_erectus_south_africa_2myr.headline: Adult Homo erectus Skull Confirms 2‑Million‑Year Presence in Southern Africa
homo_erectus_south_africa_2myr.summary: A newly described adult Homo erectus skull from Drimolen, dated 2 million years ago, pushes the species’ southern African arrival 200,000 years earlier.
highlights: Adult fossil DNH 127 dated to 2 million years, 200 kyr older than other adult specimens
18 new hominin fossils published, including Homo erectus and Paranthropus robustus remains
Paranthropus robustus shows microevolutionary increase in tooth size and chewing muscles between 2 Ma and 1.8 Ma
Homo erectus and Paranthropus robustus co‑existed, with P. robustus outnumbering Homo erectus >10:1 at Drimolen
Study appears in peer‑reviewed Annals of Human Biology (2026)

octupolar_magnetism_quantum_tech.headline: University of Toronto team spots hidden octupolar magnetism via light
octupolar_magnetism_quantum_tech.summary: Researchers used rotating light to detect chiral phonon signatures of octupolar magnetic order, offering a new optical probe for elusive quantum magnetic states.
highlights: Octupolar order exhibits eight magnetic poles, unlike conventional dipoles
Chiral phonons reveal a unique optical fingerprint when octupolar order is present
The method uses rotating light to excite pseudo‑chiral phonon modes in a crystal
Findings published in Physical Review Letters demonstrate a viable detection technique

cholesterol_lysosome_mechanism.institution: Nanyang Technological University (Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine)
cholesterol_lysosome_mechanism.headline: Cholesterol Fuels Lysosome Resilience, Safeguarding Mitochondrial Recycling
cholesterol_lysosome_mechanism.summary: Researchers discovered that cholesterol delivery to lysosome membranes preserves acidity and prevents rupture during mitophagy, linking this supply chain to brain health.
highlights: Cholesterol is shuttled from the endoplasmic reticulum to lysosomes via OSBP after PI4KIIα flags the membrane with PI4P
Blocking cholesterol transport or synthesis makes lysosomes lose acidity, become fragile, and fail to digest damaged mitochondria
Lysosomal breakdown of mitochondria releases free fatty acids that are repackaged into lipid droplets for safe storage
The study, published in Nature Communications, connects lysosomal cholesterol handling to age‑related neurodegenerative diseases

2609_39432v1.headline: Dark‑Age 21 cm Fluctuations Offer New Window on Primordial Power Spectrum
2609_39432v1.summary: Future Dark‑Age 21 cm power‑spectrum measurements could tighten constraints on inflationary models beyond the reach of current CMB data.
highlights: Dark‑Age 21 cm observations probe scales inaccessible to the CMB
Unconventional inflationary scale‑dependence can be stringently tested
Combining 21 cm data with CMB improves parameter constraints even with modest surveys

dark_galaxy_candidate_detection.headline: Dark Galaxy Candidate AGC 322753 Detected by ALFALFA and FASHI
dark_galaxy_candidate_detection.summary: Astronomers have identified a possible dark galaxy, AGC 322753, with a 2×10⁹ M⊙ HI mass and no optical counterpart down to 27.5 mag arcsec⁻².
highlights: Detected in both ALFALFA and FASHI surveys at the same recessional velocity
HI linewidth (W₅₀) ≈ 85 km s⁻¹ suggests disc-like rotation
Stellar mass limit ≤ 5×10⁷ M⊙ gives M_HI/M_ ≳ 40

dual_agn_at_z_3_273_with_175_pc_separati.headline: Chandra Confirms Dual AGN in Distant Lens MG B2016+112 at 175 pc
dual_agn_at_z_3_273_with_175_pc_separati.summary: A 175 ks Chandra observation of the z = 3.273 gravitational lens MG B2016+112 provides definitive X‑ray spectral proof of two actively accreting supermassive black holes separated by just 175 parsecs.
highlights: Separate X‑ray spectra reveal strong intrinsic absorption (N_H > 4 × 10^22 cm⁻²) in the caustic‑inside source
The system now holds the tightest confirmed dual AGN pair at high redshift
Future Euclid, SKA, Rubin and Roman surveys are expected to uncover more such compact SMBH binaries

2609_38305v1.headline: Close Pulsar Pairs Bypass Gravitational‑Wave Noise to Probe Tiny Dark‑Matter Halos
2609_38305v1.summary: Timing pulsar pairs separated by sub‑parsec distances can detect dark‑matter subhalos of ~10⁻⁶ solar masses despite a nanohertz gravitational‑wave background.
highlights: Pulsar timing arrays lose sensitivity to dark‑matter signals when a nanohertz GWB is present
Pairs spaced ~0.1 pc experience nearly identical GWB perturbations, cancelling in their residual difference
A nearby dark‑matter subhalo perturbs the two pulsars differently, remaining detectable
Sensitivity to ~10⁻⁶ solar‑mass subhalos improves by over an order of magnitude
Dense globular clusters naturally host many such close pulsar pairs

doi_10_1016_j_mayocp_2026_xxx.headline: Long‑Duration Spaceflights Increase Astronaut Hip Fracture Risk
doi_10_1016_j_mayocp_2026_xxx.summary: A new Mayo Clinic Proceedings study finds astronauts on missions over 90 days suffer significantly higher post‑flight hip fracture rates than shorter‑duration flyers or non‑astronauts.
highlights: Hip fractures rose after spaceflights longer than 90 days, despite overall fracture rates remaining unchanged
Researchers used Bayesian probabilistic modeling on a U.S. astronaut cohort to reveal the trend
NASA plans to add quantitative computed tomography scans to its bone‑health surveillance program

pulsar_glitch_starquake_model.headline: Starquake Model Shows Pulsar Glitches Triggered by Critical Stress Threshold
pulsar_glitch_starquake_model.summary: A study of 245 glitches from nine pulsars finds that glitches follow a time‑predictable pattern, occurring when stress reaches a critical threshold of ~10^34‑10^35 dyn cm⁻².
highlights: Time‑predictable model fits the observed glitch intervals better than magnitude‑predictable model
Critical stress τc estimated at (10^34‑10^35) dyn cm⁻², comparable to shear modulus of strangeon stars
Residual stress after a quake appears negligible, implying full stress release
Analysis uses the classical spring‑slider framework borrowed from seismology

new_qubit_superfluid_quantum_computer_br.headline: Superfluid Helium Qubit Promises 100‑Fold Error Reduction
new_qubit_superfluid_quantum_computer_br.summary: A proposed superfluid helium‑3 qubit could slash quantum computing error rates by about one hundred times, offering a low‑noise alternative to superconducting circuits.
highlights: SHOQ device uses charge‑neutral superfluid helium‑3 to shield qubits from electromagnetic noise
Predicted error rates are roughly 100 × lower than those of conventional superconducting qubits
Design could be integrated with existing superconducting hardware or serve as quantum memory

new_parallel_gate_entangles_diamond_qubi.headline: Parallel Gate Entangles Diamond Qubits Ten Times Faster at Room Temperature
new_parallel_gate_entangles_diamond_qubi.summary: Researchers at University of Pennsylvania demonstrated a room‑temperature parallel gate that creates a four‑qubit GHZ state in diamond in just 14.8 μs.
highlights: Four‑qubit GHZ state generated in a single 14.8 μs gate
Parallel gate fidelity of 0.92(4) versus 0.69(3) for sequential gates
Method uses a nitrogen‑vacancy center electron coupled to three carbon‑13 nuclear spins

apoe4_reversible_weakness.headline: APOE4‑Driven Vascular Damage and Protein Buildup May Be Reversible
apoe4_reversible_weakness.summary: Mount Sinai researchers showed that APOE4 transforms brain pericytes, triggers cholesterol buildup, and impairs protein clearance, but blocking TGF‑β can reverse these effects.
highlights: APOE4 converts pericytes into myofibroblast‑like cells, causing vascular fibrosis and amyloid accumulation
Blocking TGF‑β signaling restores pericyte coverage and reduces amyloid in aged APOE4 mice
APOE4‑carrying miBrains exhibit excess cholesterol in astrocytes, weakening lysosomal clearance of α‑synuclein
The miBrain platform, derived from induced pluripotent stem cells, enables rapid testing of personalized neurodegenerative

life_on_enceladus_chances_boost.headline: New Studies Boost Chances of Life in Enceladus’ Subsurface Ocean
life_on_enceladus_chances_boost.summary: Two peer‑reviewed studies show Enceladus’ salty ocean is easier to analyze and can support methane‑producing microbes, raising habitability prospects.
highlights: Droplets in Enceladus’ plume freeze slowly, separating salts such as sodium chloride from sodium carbonate into micrometer‑size
The slow‑freeze process concentrates potential biosignatures, allowing individual ice particles to be examined with existing
Laboratory simulations of Enceladus‑like alkaline (pH 10‑11), carbonate‑rich conditions enabled the archaeon Methanothermococcus

swiss_glaciers_mass_loss.headline: Swiss Glaciers Lose Nearly One‑Fifth of Mass in Five Years
swiss_glaciers_mass_loss.summary: A GLAMOS study shows Swiss glaciers shed almost 20% of their ice between 2022 and 2026, driven by record‑hot summers and minimal snowfall.
highlights: 5.5% ice volume vanished in 2026, the second‑largest melt on record
Melt rate from 2022‑2026 was more than twice any previous five‑year period
Average glacier thickness fell 2.5–4 m, with some tongues losing up to 10 m
Approximately 2.2 trillion liters of water disappeared between July and September 2026

mars_north_pole_ice_cleaner.headline: Mars' North Polar Ice Found to Be Much Cleaner Than Expected
mars_north_pole_ice_cleaner.summary: New measurements show the top layer of Mars' north polar water ice contains only about 3 percent dust, far less than the previously assumed 25 percent.
highlights: Dust by mass in the north polar cap is revised from ~25 percent to ~3 percent.
Data were derived from OMEGA, CRISM, and the Surface Stereo Imager on the Phoenix Lander.
Cleaner ice implies different climate‑dust cycles during Mars' extreme axial tilt variations.

ultra_precise_coatings_gravitational_wav.headline: ANU’s Atomic‑Scale Coatings Boost Sensitivity of Next‑Gen LIGO Detectors
ultra_precise_coatings_gravitational_wav.summary: Australian National University engineers have created atom‑level optical coatings for LIGO’s new beamsplitters, promising unprecedented detector sensitivity for faint gravitational‑wave signals.
highlights: Coatings achieve thickness uniformity within a nanometer across a 45‑centimeter glass disk
Eight custom automated systems were built to clean, measure and handle the optics without human contact
The ultralow‑reflectivity layer is over 1,000 times more effective than standard eyeglass coatings

lutetium_atomic_clock.headline: Lutetium‑176 Atomic Clock Sets New 19‑Digit Accuracy Record
lutetium_atomic_clock.summary: Physicists at the National University of Singapore unveiled a lutetium‑based clock accurate to 19 decimal places, a 41% gain over the previous best.
highlights: Accuracy reaches 19 decimal places, surpassing the former record by 41%
Uses lutetium‑176 atoms, which remain stable despite temperature swings of up to 5 °C
Hyperfine averaging technique minimizes magnetic‑field and gravitational influences

sex_like_dna_exchange_in_starving_bacter.institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
sex_like_dna_exchange_in_starving_bacter.headline: Starving E. coli Swaps DNA via Phage‑Mediated ‘Sex’ Over 100‑Fold Faster Than Mutations
sex_like_dna_exchange_in_starving_bacter.summary: Researchers at ISTA found that starving Escherichia coli use CRISPR‑Cas‑protected bacteriophages to exchange DNA, a process occurring more than a hundred times faster than spontaneous mutations.
highlights: DNA exchange is triggered by starvation‑linked gene activation.
The mechanism relies on CRISPR‑Cas immunity to repurpose phages as DNA carriers.
Exchange rates exceed spontaneous mutation rates by >100‑fold.
Resulting gene shuffling can accelerate adaptation and purge deleterious mutations.

chameleon_embryos_reveal_early_developme.headline: Veiled Chameleon Embryos Mirror Human Early Developmental Cavity
chameleon_embryos_reveal_early_developme.summary: Researchers found that veiled chameleon embryos form an internal cavity similar to humans, challenging the view that this feature is exclusive to mammals.
highlights: Veiled chameleon embryos develop an internal cavity before gastrulation, a trait previously thought unique to mammals
Study published in Nature Communications involved Rowan University, Stowers Institute, Oxford, Cambridge, and Kansas Medical
Embryos fold inward as a flat sheet, unlike the central space formation seen in human embryos

gut_mrna_tech_supercharges_vaccine_glp1_.headline: Gut‑Targeted mRNA Lipid Nanoparticles Boost Vaccines and GLP‑1 Therapy
gut_mrna_tech_supercharges_vaccine_glp1_.summary: Delivering lipid nanoparticle mRNA to specific gut regions redirects its biodistribution, enhancing vaccine efficacy and improving GLP‑1‑based metabolic treatment in mice.
highlights: Oral GI delivery of LNPs redirects them away from liver, lungs and spleen toward pancreas and lymph nodes.
Cheek administration matched or improved immune response compared to traditional subcutaneous injection.
Stomach delivery of GLP‑1 mRNA lowered blood glucose in mouse models, showing metabolic benefit.
High‑dose gastric delivery proved safe with no toxicity observed.

room_temp_entangled_glass_speck.headline: Room‑Temperature Entanglement Achieved Between Light and Levitating Glass Nanoparticle
room_temp_entangled_glass_speck.summary: Physicists at the University of Florence entangled the motion of a 100‑nm glass nanosphere with light using a two‑color optical tweezer, all at room temperature.
highlights: Entanglement observed between the nanosphere’s position‑momentum and the light’s quadratures
Two lasers – a red‑detuned cooling beam and a blue‑detuned entangling beam – formed a two‑color tweezer
The entangled light exits the cavity, enabling potential transmission through optical networks

2610_00485v1.headline: Weak Lensing Tightens Limits on Primordial Magnetic Fields
2610_00485v1.summary: Using N-body simulations and weak‑lensing convergence spectra, researchers set sub‑nanogauss upper bounds on early‑universe magnetic fields.
highlights: Upper limits of B₁Mpc < 1.6 nG, 1.0 nG, and 0.8 nG for ℓₘₐₓ = 5000, 10000, 20000 respectively
Models with spectral index n_B = ‑2.1 are more tightly constrained than those with n_B = ‑2.7
No strong degeneracy found between magnetic‑field parameters and intrinsic‑alignment or baryon‑feedback effects

grb_cgm_quasar_nebulae.headline: Dense, Clumpy CGM Around High‑Redshift Quasars Defies Current Simulations
grb_cgm_quasar_nebulae.summary: MUSE observations of quasar Lyα nebulae at z ≈ 3.5 reveal far more high‑surface‑brightness gas than predicted by leading cosmological simulations.
highlights: MUSE data show Lyα surface‑brightness covering fractions far exceeding DaLya, COLIBRE m6 and HELLO predictions
Observed CGM densities reach ≥10 cm⁻³ within 50–200 ckpc of quasars
Simulated cold‑gas PDFs are log‑normal with median ~10⁻² cm⁻³ and clumping factors 16–102, far lower than required by observations

desi_bispectrum_analysis.headline: Joint DESI DR1 Power Spectrum and Bispectrum Analysis Tightens Cosmological Parameters
desi_bispectrum_analysis.summary: A combined full‑shape study of DESI DR1 LRG and QSO data shows the bispectrum improves constraints on dark matter density and matter fluctuation amplitude by up to 20 %.
highlights: Bispectrum inclusion boosts cold dark matter density precision by 9‑18 % and σ₈ by 8‑20 % in single‑tracer analyses
Combined LRG sample sees 15 % and 10 % reductions respectively, with all tracers together improving by 6 % and 4 %
Analysis uses one‑loop power spectrum and tree‑level bispectrum modeled via Effective Field Theory of Large‑Scale Structure

protocluster_metallicities_at_z_7.headline: JWST Reveals Elevated Metallicity in z≈6.93 Protocluster Lyman‑α Emitters
protocluster_metallicities_at_z_7.summary: Using JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, researchers measured direct‑method metallicities of six Lyman‑α emitters in the LAGER‑z7OD1 protocluster at redshift 6.93 during reionization.
highlights: Five secure detections of the [O III] λ4363 auroral line give 12+log(O/H) values between 7.2 and 8.0.
Stacked spectrum yields a metallicity of 12+log(O/H)=7.76±0.06, about 0.26 dex higher than typical LAEs at similar redshift.
Mass‑metallicity relation slope γ=0.232±0.214 places these galaxies below the established MZR for normal galaxies.
Results suggest accelerated assembly in the overdense region while pristine gas inflow dilutes the interstellar medium.

poisson_isocurvature_gws.headline: Poisson Isocurvature Fluctuations Boost Induced Gravitational Waves in Early‑Universe Transition
poisson_isocurvature_gws.summary: A sudden shift from early matter domination to radiation reveals how Poisson isocurvature perturbations from primordial black hole evaporation shape induced gravitational‑wave spectra.
highlights: Poisson isocurvature perturbations arise from discrete PBH number‑density fluctuations
Induced GW tensor power spectrum depends only on scalar two‑point correlations
Higher‑order scalar correlations first appear in the GW tensor bispectrum
Scale‑dependent bispectrum amplitudes could differentiate PBH scenarios from other mechanisms

underwater_umbrellas_coral_reefs.headline: Underwater Umbrellas Shield Vulnerable Caribbean Corals From Heat Stress
underwater_umbrellas_coral_reefs.summary: Custom-made shade structures reduced bleaching in brain corals during a record‑heat summer, offering a temporary, scalable protection method.
highlights: 20 nylon‑cloth umbrellas were deployed over 10 colonies of Pseudodiploria clivosa and Colpophyllia natans in the Florida Keys
Shaded corals experienced 60% less light and retained more color than unshaded controls during the second‑highest temperature
The experiment showed no change in algal density or species composition between shaded and control groups

lowest_mass_double_neutron_star.headline: FAST discovers lowest‑mass double neutron star system, testing Einstein’s gravity
lowest_mass_double_neutron_star.summary: Astronomers using FAST have measured the smallest combined mass for a double neutron star, confirming orbital decay predictions of general relativity.
highlights: PSR J1856−0039 has a 2.36‑hour orbit, the second shortest among known DNS systems
Combined neutron‑star mass is the lowest ever recorded for a DNS pair
Measured three post‑Keplerian parameters match general‑relativistic predictions

no_longer_just_north_and_south_a_new_mat.headline: Altermagnetism Demonstrated in Co₁/₄TaSe₂ Layered Crystal
no_longer_just_north_and_south_a_new_mat.summary: Physicists at University of Central Florida have experimentally confirmed altermagnetism in Co₁/₄TaSe₂, a layered material that splits spin without stray magnetic fields.
highlights: Co₁/₄TaSe₂ crystals were grown at >900 °C for two weeks
Angle‑resolved photoemission spectroscopy revealed spin‑polarized band splitting
The material combines spin‑splitting ability of ferromagnets with zero stray fields of antiferromagnets

asteroid_bennu_has_an_identity_crisis_an.headline: Jupiter’s Early Gravitational Grip Explains Asteroid Bennu’s Mixed Origins
asteroid_bennu_has_an_identity_crisis_an.summary: New isotopic analysis of Bennu’s sample shows it carries signatures of both inner‑solar‑system and outer‑solar‑system material, likely due to Jupiter’s early influence.
highlights: Bennu’s iron isotopes match inner‑solar‑system NC asteroids while titanium and chromium align with outer‑solar‑system CC asteroids
Manganese‑53 dating places Bennu’s formation just 2 million years after the first solids condensed
Jupiter’s massive early presence created pressure ridges that trapped chondrules and formed dust‑traffic‑jam layers at the ice

chip_based_laser_stable_no_active_contro.headline: EPFL’s Chip Laser Stays Locked Across Full Current Range Without Active Control
chip_based_laser_stable_no_active_contro.summary: Researchers at EPFL have created a photonic integrated laser that maintains ultra‑stable frequency across 154‑300 mA drive currents without any active electronic feedback.
highlights: Self‑injection locking reduces frequency noise by over 5,000× compared with a free‑running laser
Intrinsic linewidth remains below 10 hertz across the entire tested current range
Mode‑hop‑free frequency chirps exceed 1.5 gigahertz while the laser stays locked

aurochs_genetic_extinction_study.headline: Genetic bottleneck and human hunting drove aurochs extinction in Scandinavia
aurochs_genetic_extinction_study.summary: New Holocene study shows that reduced genetic diversity, intense hunting, and habitat change together caused the aurochs’ disappearance in northern Europe.
highlights: Aurochs arrived in Scandinavia 11,700 years ago but suffered a sharp genetic bottleneck during northward migration
Isolation after the Danish‑Swedish straits flooded ~8,000 years ago coincided with intense human hunting
Habitat shift to dense forests led to the final loss of Swedish aurochs by ~6,500 years ago

the_ancestors_of_today_s_indigenous_peop.headline: Ancient DNA Shows Ancestors of Modern Indigenous Peoples Arrived Near End of Last Glacial Maximum
the_ancestors_of_today_s_indigenous_peop.summary: Genetic analysis indicates the migration that founded today’s Indigenous peoples entered the Americas no earlier than 21,000 years ago, near the peak of the Last Glacial Maximum.
highlights: Study of ~250 ancient genomes narrows entry window to 21,000‑14,000 years ago
Researchers used data from the Anzick‑1 child (12,800 yr) and other early genomes
Findings align with archaeological evidence of coastal migration during the LGM

ocean_warming_method.headline: New Method Shows Double-Digit Gaps Between Ocean Warming and Climate Models
ocean_warming_method.summary: Researchers at the University of Bonn combined buoy data with satellite sea‑level measurements to reveal that individual ocean basins warm up to double‑digit percentages more than climate models predict.
highlights: Indian Ocean absorbed unusually large heat from 2005‑2015
Pacific, Atlantic and Indian oceans each took roughly one‑third of extra heat over the past 20 years
Method calculates regional thermal‑expansion coefficients, correcting a common uniform‑assumption error

uranium_triple_bond_nature_chemistry_202.headline: Uranium Forms Rare Triple Bond with Carbon in First Isolable Fischer‑Type Carbyne
uranium_triple_bond_nature_chemistry_202.summary: Researchers at the University of Manchester have synthesized and characterized the first stable uranium‑carbon triple‑bond compound, expanding actinide chemistry.
highlights: Uranium‑carbon triple bond measured at 2.379 Å
Synthesis used a novel carbon‑atom transfer reagent
Structure confirmed by single‑crystal X‑ray diffraction and magnetometry

cosmic_ray_thunderstorms.headline: GRAPES-3 Muon Telescope Reveals Electric Fields Inside Thunderstorms via Cosmic Rays
cosmic_ray_thunderstorms.summary: Researchers used the GRAPES-3 muon telescope to detect variations in muon flux, uncovering gigavolt potentials in thunderclouds and explaining a pronounced east‑west detection bias.
highlights: Measured thunderstorm electric potentials up to 1.3 gigavolts, far exceeding previous direct observations.
Detected 487 thunderstorm events (2011‑2020), with 81.5 % appearing eastward versus 13.7 % westward.
Simulations show direction‑dependent muon charge ratio of 1.37 (east) versus 1.14 (west), causing the asymmetry.
The geomagnetic east‑west effect alters cosmic‑ray muon flux, enabling GRAPES-3 to probe atmospheric electricity from the ground.

mirror_image_crystals_reverse_the_direct.headline: Mirror‑Image 2D Perovskite Crystals Reverse Light‑Driven Spin Currents
mirror_image_crystals_reverse_the_direct.summary: Researchers at Science Tokyo showed that bulk circular photogalvanic effect in chiral 2D hybrid perovskites flips direction with light handedness, confirming a bulk origin.
highlights: Circular photogalvanic effect (CPGE) observed in 2D organic‑inorganic hybrid perovskite crystals
Photocurrent direction reverses when using right‑ or left‑handed circularly polarized light at normal incidence
Chiral enantiomeric crystals produce opposite CPGE signs, proving bulk polarity controls the current

embryo_model_validation.headline: University of Sydney devises benchmark to gauge lab‑grown human blastoid fidelity
embryo_model_validation.summary: Researchers created a reference map from over 14,000 single‑cell transcriptomes to objectively assess how closely stem‑cell‑derived blastoid models mimic early human embryos.
highlights: Four leading blastoid protocols were systematically compared against a comprehensive embryonic reference map
Some models reproduced all three major lineages, but none fully recapitulated a natural blastocyst
The computational framework and datasets are publicly released for global benchmarking

sea_monkeys_turbulence_rule_2026.headline: Brine Shrimp Reveal How to Reverse Energy Flow in 2D Turbulence
sea_monkeys_turbulence_rule_2026.summary: Researchers at the University of Pittsburgh showed that the orientation of tiny brine shrimp can flip the direction of energy cascade in a two‑dimensional turbulent fluid.
highlights: The shrimp’s swimming angle relative to flow determines whether energy moves from small to large scales or vice‑versa.
A simple angled obstacle or array of rods can steer the energy flux in the laboratory tank.
Numerical simulations by the University of Turin confirmed the experimental inverse cascade effect.
Potential applications include low‑energy pollution control and more efficient mixing in drug design.

scientists_discover_first_type_i_superco.headline: First Type‑I Superconductor YbSb₂ Found to Break Time‑Reversal Symmetry
scientists_discover_first_type_i_superco.summary: Researchers at IISC‑Bhopal demonstrated that YbSb₂, a type‑I superconductor, spontaneously generates internal magnetic fields, revealing broken time‑reversal symmetry.
highlights: YbSb₂ crystals exhibit type‑I magnetic behavior, fully expelling external fields
Muon spin rotation measurements detected spontaneous internal fields below the superconducting transition
The observed symmetry breaking suggests an internally antisymmetric nonunitary triplet (INT) state
Calculations indicate possible gapless Majorana surface modes, hinting at topological superconductivity

animal_evolution_earlier.headline: Animals May Have Originated 200 Million Years Earlier Than Fossils Show
animal_evolution_earlier.summary: A new study using Mongolian microfossils and molecular clocks suggests animal life began 800‑700 million years ago, far before the first clear fossils.
highlights: Mongolian Kheseen Biota, 40 million years younger than Weng'an, lacks animal fossils despite excellent preservation
Molecular‑clock analysis pushes animal origin back by ~200 million years to 800‑700 Ma
Chemical biomarkers hint at sponge‑like organisms existing 650 Ma
Early animals likely small, soft‑bodied, and missed by fossilization during Cryogenian Snowball Earth events

agrivoltaics_magenta_panels.headline: Magenta Solar Panels Boost Broccoli Growth While Generating Renewable Power
agrivoltaics_magenta_panels.summary: Semi‑transparent magenta panels increased broccoli’s sunlight use efficiency 4.5‑fold, matching yields despite a 25‑day longer maturation period.
highlights: Broccoli under magenta panels grew as large as open‑field crops while using sunlight 4.5‑times more efficiently
The 20 m × 20 m prototype generated electricity and filtered blue‑red light to enhance photosynthesis
Two panel transparencies produced similar crop performance, indicating flexibility in design

changes_to_platinum_surface_chemistry_bo.headline: Halide Choice Alters Platinum Surface, Boosts Solar Hydrogen Yield
changes_to_platinum_surface_chemistry_bo.summary: EPFL researchers found that using bromide or iodide precursors for platinum deposition eliminates surface poisoning, raising hydrogen evolution to a 17% quantum yield at 700 nm.
highlights: Chloroplatinate precursors leave Pt–Cl species that poison active sites, suppressing hydrogen production
Bromo- and iodoplatinate precursors reduce more readily, avoiding poisoning and improving performance
Modified Pt surfaces achieve an apparent quantum yield of 17% at 700 nm, among the highest for organic semiconductor nanoparticles

hypernovas_real.headline: New Models Challenge Existence of Hypernovas in Stellar Chemistry
hypernovas_real.summary: Mathematical models suggest that oddball halo stars can be explained by ordinary supernovae, casting doubt on previously claimed hypernova origins.
highlights: Models accounting for asymmetric element mixing reproduce observed ratios in Milky Way halo stars
The study appears in the September issue of Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
Ralph Schönrich (University College London) says the evidence for hypernovas is now seriously challenged
Anna Frebel (MIT) notes the findings remind astronomers to avoid claiming uniqueness
Adam Burrows (Princeton University) confirms irregular mixing is known among supernova researchers

ultrafast_xray_azobenzene_switch.headline: Ultrafast X‑rays Capture First‑Picosecond Shape Shift of Azobenzene
ultrafast_xray_azobenzene_switch.summary: Using PAL‑XFEL, researchers observed that azobenzene’s central nitrogen atoms twist within a few picoseconds after light absorption, while its benzene rings stay nearly static.
highlights: Coordinated motion of the two nitrogen atoms initiates the trans‑to‑cis isomerization
Benzene rings remain largely unchanged during the initial reaction stage
Ultrafast X‑ray liquidography separated azobenzene signal from methanol solvent

enzyme_beads_sustainable_chemistry.headline: Enzyme Beads Offer Storable, Efficient Platform for Sustainable Chemical Production
enzyme_beads_sustainable_chemistry.summary: KIT researchers created millimeter‑sized all‑enzyme beads that act as both catalyst and material, enabling reusable, transportable biocatalysis for fine chemicals and pharmaceuticals.
highlights: Complementary enzyme binding modules self‑assemble into porous protein beads via freeze‑drying.
Hybrid beads combine enzymes with Escherichia coli cells, retaining activity after five months dry storage.
Beads function in continuous‑flow reactors, demonstrating modular scalability for diverse reactions.

tomato_wilt_virus_clone.headline: Texas A&M Develops First U.S. Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus Clone
tomato_wilt_virus_clone.summary: Researchers at Texas A&M AgriLife Research have engineered the nation’s inaugural infectious clone of tomato spotted wilt virus, enabling faster breeding of resistant tomatoes and peppers.
highlights: The clone reproduces the full‑length TSWV genome as an infectious cDNA copy
It allows unlimited virus production for efficient plant inoculation
Breeders can now screen for resistance traits more rapidly, cutting development time
TSWV causes an estimated $100 million in annual crop losses in the southeastern U.S.

superconductor_vacuum_enhancement.headline: Engineered Vacuum Boosts NbSe₂ Superconductivity by Up to 5.4%
superconductor_vacuum_enhancement.summary: Quantum vacuum fluctuations amplified in a terahertz dark cavity raise the critical temperature of six‑layer NbSe₂ by as much as 5.4%.
highlights: Critical temperature increased by up to 5.4% in a six‑layer NbSe₂ device
Critical current and critical magnetic field show significant enhancement near the transition
Effect peaks at a resonant cavity frequency, confirming coupling to dark‑cavity modes

tlr4_undruggable_site_protein_design.headline: Computer‑Designed Protein Blocks Inflammatory Signaling by Targeting TLR4’s Membrane Core
tlr4_undruggable_site_protein_design.summary: Researchers at Scripps Research created a synthetic protein that binds the transmembrane region of Toll‑like receptor 4, sharply reducing NF‑κB inflammation in human cells.
highlights: Designed protein “Design‑6” showed strongest binding to TLR4’s membrane‑spanning segment and lowered NF‑κB activity.
Computational workflow screened nine candidates, with eight confirming membrane association via a light‑up assay.
Study reveals the transmembrane region as an active driver of TLR4 signaling, opening a new drug‑target class.

chang_e6_magnetic_mineral.headline: Chang’e-6 Lunar Soil Reveals Unexpected Magnetic γ‑Fe Nanoparticles
chang_e6_magnetic_mineral.summary: Scientists analyzing Chang’e-6 impact‑glass samples discovered nanoscale γ‑Fe that preserves a stable magnetic signal, offering a new record of the Moon’s ancient magnetic field.
highlights: γ‑Fe identified for the first time in natural lunar samples
Nanoparticles retain a single‑vortex magnetic state under external fields
Impact‑glass cooling and carbon impurities may stabilize high‑temperature γ‑Fe

true_polar_wander_constraints.headline: Ancient Sea‑Level Maps Reveal Multiple Episodes of Rapid True Polar Wander
true_polar_wander_constraints.summary: Researchers used 10‑million‑year sea‑level reconstructions to identify four intervals of fast true polar wander over the past 320 million years.
highlights: Four rapid true polar wander events detected between 200‑190 Ma, 150‑140 Ma, 100‑90 Ma, and 30‑20 Ma
Sea‑level patterns show simultaneous rises and falls in opposite hemispheres, matching model predictions
Study led by Mathew Domeier at the University of Oslo, published in Science
Digital continental flooding maps provided a novel proxy for tracking mantle‑spin axis shifts

milky_way_progenitor_galaxies.headline: Simulations Reveal Milky Way Began as Thousands of Early Galaxies
milky_way_progenitor_galaxies.summary: New MEGATRON simulations suggest the Milky Way formed from a web of thousands of tiny galaxies, predicting their appearance to Hubble and James Webb telescopes.
highlights: Thousands of proto‑galaxies merged over the first billion years to create today’s spiral disk.
Simulations include detailed non‑equilibrium physics, gravity, radiation and chemistry, a first for Milky Way models.
Population III supernovae explain why iron abundance stops decreasing in the faintest early galaxies.
Model predicts star‑less “galaxies” that still emit light, offering new observational targets for JWST.

resistant_bacteria_vulnerabilities.headline: Targeting Energy, Phage Resistance, and Toxin Loading in Superbugs
resistant_bacteria_vulnerabilities.summary: NTU scientists unveiled a metabolism‑blocking compound for Mycobacterium abscessus, revealed phage‑resistance mechanisms, and mapped the toxin‑loading apparatus of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
highlights: A novel inhibitor binds a pocket in M. abscessus cytochrome b bcc oxidase, cutting ATP production and achieving a 2‑log kill
Loss of glycopeptidolipids drives M. abscessus to a rough, more virulent form that evades bacteriophage attack.
Cryo‑EM revealed the Type VI Secretion System loads toxins into Hcp rings, forming a harpoon‑like tube that delivers multiple

kdm4a_drives_tgct_metastasis.headline: KDM4A fuels testicular germ cell tumor spread via STAT1‑CCL3 signaling
kdm4a_drives_tgct_metastasis.summary: Researchers show that the histone demethylase KDM4A drives metastasis of testicular germ cell tumors by activating STAT1‑dependent CCL3 transcription and the PI3K/AKT pathway.
highlights: KDM4A is uniquely over‑expressed in TGCTs among all histone demethylases
Knocking down KDM4A reduces TGCT cell migration, invasion, and lung metastasis in mice
KDM4A demethylates H3K9me3 at the CCL3 promoter, enabling STAT1‑driven transcription
CCL3 activation triggers PI3K/AKT signaling, promoting focal adhesion turnover
Targeting KDM4A may offer a new therapeutic avenue for metastatic TGCT
